Agreement to run a 48-hour benchmark on a sampled workload and follow up with sizing and pricing for a 3-month pilot.
topics: deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-14 15:30 UTC | Duration: 61m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Head of ML, Bluebridge), Ethan Clark (Platform Lead), Leila Ahmed (Security Engineer)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna do a quick intro and then dive into the POC scope — particularly how you want to weigh hosted versus dedicated or private deployment. Priya will cover the technical bits.
[00:18] Maria Gomez: Thanks Jordan. Quick context — we run a mix of near-real-time triage flows (user-facing chat, ~50 qps peak) and nightly batch embedding jobs that run against the EMR dataset. Latency for the chat path is the immediate blocker — we want p95 < 120ms ideally, p99 under 300ms is acceptable. Also strict PHI controls.
[00:36] Priya Nair: Got it. That sounds like two different workload profiles which may push you to hybrid mode. A hosted Redwood API is easiest to get started, but Dedicated or Private gives you more isolation for PHI and stricter network controls. We'll lay out the tradeoffs.
[00:55] Ethan Clark: Quick question on throughput: our peak chat traffic is 50 qps but bursts up to 125 qps during outages. Nightly embedding batch is big — roughly 200k docs, but it's chunked across jobs. Cost is also a major concern; we have a fixed budget for the pilot.
[01:15] Jordan Lee: Thanks Ethan. For sizing we typically look at tokens/sec and concurrency. For 50 qps conversational sessions with average prompt+response of 600 tokens, we can approximate concurrent token throughput. We'll produce a sizing doc after we get your sample traces.
[01:34] Leila Ahmed: Security: we run HIPAA; we need SOC2 plus audited KMS for key management, audit logs stored for 1 year, and VPC peering or private link for the dedicated/private options. Also, can Redwood do an on-prem install?
[01:52] Priya Nair: We support Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packages). On-prem is possible but increases pilot timeline — you'll need infra + access to ops. For Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools with VPC connectivity and customer-managed KMS integration. Hosted has standard encryption in transit/rest but we can sign an addendum and discuss data retention rules.
[02:15] Maria Gomez: For the POC success criteria, we want: 1) realtime chat p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms for 95% of traffic; 2) embedding batch throughput that finishes under our nightly window (4 hours); 3) no PHI exfiltration and audit logs ingestion into our SIEM; 4) cost per 1M tokens under $X (we'll share target).
[02:38] Jordan Lee: That's clear. We'll map those into measurable benchmarks. Priya, can you outline what the 48-hour benchmark will capture?
[02:47] Priya Nair: Sure — baseline with Hosted first using anonymized traces, measuring cold-start latencies, p50/p95/p99, streaming tail behavior, and throughput on sustained load. Then we can run Dedicated sizing runs with different batch sizes and quantization profiles. Key things: KV cache hit rates, prefix caching impact, and model variant fallback behavior. We'll also simulate bursts.
[03:12] Ethan Clark: How do you simulate our embedding job? It's not a uniform doc size — some docs are large (10k tokens) and others tiny. That variance matters.
[03:22] Priya Nair: We ask for a small sample dataset — minimally redacted — with distribution of doc lengths. We then replay the job with the same batching strategy. For embeddings, quantized models plus batched requests can significantly lower cost.
[03:35] Maria Gomez: When would we see Dedicated pricing and capacity recommendations?
[03:39] Jordan Lee: We'll aim to send a draft by end of week once we have your sample traces. The initial Dedicated sizing will include recommended GPU profiles, reserved vCPU/RAM, and expected tokens/sec with headroom for bursts.
[03:54] Leila Ahmed: About audit logs — we need to ensure all requests are logged with request IDs and user mapping. Can Redwood stream logs to our Splunk instance or S3?
[04:05] Priya Nair: Yes, we support log streaming to S3 and direct syslog/Splunk integrations in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we can provide access to tenant-level logs and deliver periodic exports; streaming is available as an add-on.
[04:19] [crosstalk] Maria Gomez: And the encryption at rest — do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:23] Priya Nair: Yes, KMS/HSM integration is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we offer managed keys but can discuss BYOK for enterprise contracts.
[04:35] Jordan Lee: Let's dig into tradeoffs briefly. Hosted: fastest onboarding, lower up-front cost, but less control for PHI. Dedicated: reserved capacity, better predictability, network isolation, and KMS integration. Private/on-prem: maximum control and compliance but longer lead time and higher ops burden.
[04:55] Ethan Clark: Pragmatically, we might start Hosted to iterate on prompts, then migrate to Dedicated for the pilot. Any pitfalls in that path?
[05:04] Priya Nair: Cold-start differences and throughput tuning can differ across modes — e.g., Dedicated can be tuned for lower latency with different kernel/compiler options. We recommend running the same benchmark across modes to identify regressions. Also watch for model variant parity (same weights/quantization).
[05:27] Maria Gomez: For acceptance criteria, do you need accuracy metrics? We have sensitive scoring thresholds — false positive rate in the triage model can't spike more than 2%.
[05:36] Priya Nair: We'll capture quality via your eval set. Run A/B comparisons during the pilot; Redwood Optimize can surface regressions against baseline prompts. We'll include automatic quality monitoring as part of the POC.
[05:52] Jordan Lee: Timeline check: You mentioned wanting to kick the pilot by Sep 8. That gives ~3 weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:58] Ethan Clark: We're constrained — infra approvals take time. Maybe Sep 22 is safer unless we do Hosted first which is quicker.
[06:06] Leila Ahmed: Security review cycles are often 2–3 weeks. If you want Private or Dedicated, procurement and legal will add time.
[06:14] Jordan Lee: Actionable plan: 1) Bluebridge provide sample traces and minimal redacted data by Aug 17; 2) Redwood runs 48-hour hosted benchmark Aug 19–21; 3) Redwood delivers benchmark results, Dedicated sizing, and pricing by Aug 22; 4) if Dedicated looks good, target pilot start Sep 22. Does that align?
[06:33] Maria Gomez: Yes. Add a security artifact handoff to that list.
[06:37] Jordan Lee: Noted. Leila, Redwood will send SOC2 and the infra network diagram.
[06:41] Leila Ahmed: Also we need to know about data residency — some subsets of the dataset must remain in EU. Do you have region guarantees?
[06:49] Priya Nair: We support region pinning for Hosted in certain cloud regions; Dedicated and Private can be deployed in EU-only regions. We'll mark that as a requirement in the sizing doc.
[07:01] Ethan Clark: Can you explain the fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is saturated? Do requests fail or route to a cheaper model?
[07:10] Priya Nair: Smart routing policies can fall back to lower-cost model variants or cross-region capacity, depending on your policy. For strict SLAs we recommend reserved capacity plus burst capacity. We'll document options and costs in the proposal.
[07:26] Maria Gomez: On measuring p99, how do you handle very low-frequency tail events? We care about real p99 under production.
[07:36] Priya Nair: We'll include both synthetic stress tests and a production-like replay. For tails, we instrument with tracing and include warmup scripts to reduce cold-starts. Also look at continuous prefix caching to reduce latency on repeated prompts.
[07:56] Jordan Lee: Any concerns about model licensing or weights? You're using an open model internally?
[08:03] Maria Gomez: We run a mix; some open weights and some proprietary fine-tuned models. If we push private models to Redwood, what's the onboarding story?
[08:13] Priya Nair: For Private and Dedicated you can bring-your-own-model. We'll help with conversion and quantization guidance. For Hosted, we'd need to discuss secure model upload and access controls. We'll add that as an item.
[08:28] [brief pause]
[08:36] Ethan Clark: Regarding cost targets, our finance team expects a not-to-exceed for the pilot. Jordan, you'll share an initial estimate?
[08:43] Jordan Lee: Yes — after we size Dedicated and run the hosted baseline we'll provide a per-token and monthly reserved estimate with scenarios.
[08:52] Maria Gomez: Can we request a canary rollout plan in the pilot? If we deploy Dedicated, we want canary routing to real traffic with automatic rollback.
[08:59] Priya Nair: Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback policies — we can demo that. We'll also show traces in Redwood Console so you can see token-level cost breakdowns.
[09:12] Leila Ahmed: Final security nit: do you sign BAA for HIPAA?
[09:16] Jordan Lee: We can — enterprise contracts include BAA. We'll loop in legal.
[09:21] Maria Gomez: Cool. I want to emphasize acceptance criteria in plain terms — performance, completion of nightly embedding in 4 hours, security sign-off, and cost target. If those are met, pilot is a success.
[09:35] Priya Nair: We'll map those to metrics in the POC test plan. For the embedding job we'll provide throughput graphs and an SLO pass/fail for the nightly window.
[09:47] Jordan Lee: OK, let's recap the next steps...
[09:50] [recap given: match action items and next steps already recorded]
[10:02] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the benchmark plan and calendar invites for the technical deep-dive and the security handoff.
[10:10] Maria Gomez: Thank you, talk soon.
[10:12] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hear of acronyms (e.g., "KMS" recorded correctly mostly, small mis-hears around model names), filler words preserved, some speaker attribution may be imperfect when crosstalk occurs.
